summary: Focused independent review of the updated Release Intelligence v2.0.0-GA GOLDEN BUILD ZIP SHA256 6b3529b31ff5bc2bea8a13b9aea5dadea4a0fbfdfde1e2b80604b06048b57be2. All 29 packaged files byte-match source. Monthly evaluation accepts safe plain prose and summary aliases, retains substantive current-paragraph checks, and rejects forged evidence keys. Missing citations or absent/invalid prior context generate visible notes; unsafe prior content is omitted rather than applied. The 360-character/60-word preference now has a 500-character/85-word hard limit. Readiness-direction language no longer incorrectly asserts achieved readiness. Failed generation still preserves the editor. The seven metrics share one collapsible, keyboard-focusable horizontal strip with existing filter/chip actions retained. Independently executed three targeted current-prose, readiness, and failed-output tests successfully; no broad suite was run. No blocking issues found. Overall application risk remains High under the existing rubric assessment.
caveats: Missing delivery citations no longer prevent applying a valid current paragraph. Visible evidence-coverage notes require human review; acceptance does not establish that every work item was represented.
Optional historical text that fails validation is omitted. Users must inspect the visible notes and saved history when historical context matters.
The hard paragraph limits are intentionally broader than the preferred compact format. Larger accepted paragraphs can occupy more display lines.

Factual and temporal validation remains heuristic rather than a proof of grounding. Goals, completion, release, production, recovery plans, and current versus historical states still require review against source evidence.

Existing Slack prepare/copy-only and unverified native paste/identity behavior, rich-text ordering limits, usage completeness, cache/cancellation, refresh concurrency, journal growth, non-atomic updates, host/catalog/history limits, sharing, and unavailable live list-column metadata caveats remain.

This was a fast focused source/artifact review with three independently executed targeted tests. The implementing agent reported 48 focused monthly/AI/grounding tests and the seven-tile/correction/editor-preservation/save browser check passed. Those broader focused checks and actual native/SDK production-model or hosted-browser behavior were not independently verified; no full test suite was rerun.
